definitions.explanation: The lowest above-ground level of a building. Japanese floor numbering starts at {一階|いっかい} for the level you enter from the street, matching American "first floor" and British "ground floor."

examples.japanese: {一階|いっかい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{待|ま}っています→待つ：00469_matsu⟧。
examples.english: I'll be waiting on the first floor.

examples.japanese: ⟦{受付|うけつけ}→受付：01325_uketsuke⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一階|いっかい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Reception is on the first floor.

examples.japanese: {一階|いっかい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦レストラン→レストラン：01048_resutoran⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書店|しょてん}→書店：04205_shoten⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}っている→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: The first floor has a restaurant and a bookstore in it.

notes:
⟦{階|かい}→階：01034_kai⟧ is the counter for floors of a building. With ⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧ it undergoes sound change to ⟦いっ→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧い. The kanji ⟦{階|かい}→階：01034_kai⟧ also appears in ⟦{階段|かいだん}→階段：00782_kaidan⟧ (stairs) and {階下|かいか} (downstairs).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一階|いっかい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{降|お}りる→降りる：00568_oriru⟧: to go down to the first floor
- {一階|いっかい}⟦{部分|ぶぶん}→部分：03715_bubun⟧: first-floor section
- {一階|いっかい}{建|だ}て: one-storey (building)

FORMS:
- ⟦{二階|にかい}→二階：27513_nikai⟧: second floor
- ⟦{地下|ちか}→地下：03429_chika⟧{一階|いっかい}: first basement level (B1)
- ⟦{最|さい}{上階|じょうかい}→最上階：30428_saijoukai⟧: top floor

WATCH OUT:
⟦{一回|いっかい}→一回：08925_ikkai⟧ "one time" sounds identical but uses ⟦{回|かい}→回：00957_kai⟧ (counter for times). Context normally distinguishes them.
